_summary.pentagon_jbook_findings: All 6 J-Book-grounded claims returned NOT_FOUND. Per heuristic §7, NOT_FOUND is a corpus-coverage gap, not a red flag. v1 J-Book corpus (410 PEs) is heavily weighted toward DARPA / MDA / SOCOM / USAF RDT&E / Space Force RDT&E volumes — small-UAS procurement (Switchblade, Puma, Raven, SRR) and Navy submarine-launched UAS are NOT seeded. Cross-verification via USAspending confirms AVAV's named programs (Switchblade $406M FY20-22 + $128M April-2024; Puma $323M Ukraine 2023) received material funding through cutoff. The framework's PRIMARY divergence test (forward J-Book unfunded vs claimed program revenue) is INAPPLICABLE here because the relevant PEs/procurement lines are not in the v1 corpus. SECONDARY tests (USAspending forward-pipeline, insider-vs-calendar, earmark) all return PASS-equivalent.
_summary.coverage_gap_recommendation: To make the J-Book divergence test active for AVAV-class small-UAS primes, extend programs.json with the relevant Army procurement P-40 line items (Switchblade / LMAMS RDT&E + Procurement PEs; SRR Increment 1; Family of Systems Carrier) and the appropriate Navy submarine-launched UAS PEs.
